headline: This law makes permanent several federal technology oversight rules and extends a federal data center consolidation program through fiscal year 2020.
what_it_does: It removes the expiration date from parts of a 2014 defense law that govern how federal agencies manage their computer and technology spending. OMB must keep a public list of major technology investments with cost, schedule, and performance data. Agency chief information officers and program managers must review investments that have carried a high risk rating for four quarters in a row. The law also extends the Federal Data Center Consolidation Initiative, which aims to reduce the number of federal data centers, through fiscal year 2020.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that buy or run information technology
who_it_affects.how: They must keep their major technology investments reported publicly and run risk reviews on investments that stay at high risk for four quarters.

who_it_affects.group: Agency chief information officers and program managers
who_it_affects.how: They are responsible for carrying out the risk management reviews of high-risk technology investments.

who_it_affects.group: Federal data center operators and staff
who_it_affects.how: The data center consolidation effort continues through fiscal year 2020, so agencies keep working to combine or close data centers.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who track federal spending
who_it_affects.how: They can view a public list of major federal technology investments with cost, schedule, and performance information.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 21, 2017; the removal of the expiration dates and the data center extension apply from that date, with the data center initiative running through fiscal year 2020.
